text_en: The Euro is introduced as the official physical currency in the Eurozone countries. The first physical transactions are carried out on Réunion. The former currencies of all the countries that use the Euro cease to be legal tender on February 28.

The Boston Globe publishes results of an investigation leading to the criminal prosecutions of five Roman Catholic priests and bringing widespread attention to the sexual abuse of minors by Catholic clergy.
The United Nations and Sierra Leone create a joint Special Court for Sierra Leone to prosecute the Revolutionary United Front.
Mount Nyiragongo erupts in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, displacing an estimated 400,000 people.
The Sierra Leone Civil War comes to a conclusion with the defeat of the Revolutionary United Front by government forces.
In American football, Tom Brady's victory in the Tuck Rule Game causes a national controversy.
American president George W. Bush defines an "axis of evil," consisting of Iran, Iraq, and North Korea in his State of the Union Address.
2002 Afyon earthquake: A 6.0 magnitude earthquake strikes Afyonkarahisar Province, Turkey, killing 41 people and damaging thousands of buildings.
NASA launches the Reuven Ramaty High Energy Solar Spectroscopic Imager as part of the Explorers Program.
24 – The 2002 Winter Olympics are held in Salt Lake City, Utah.
NASA's 2001 Mars Odyssey space probe begins to map the surface of Mars using its thermal emission imaging system.
UNITA guerrilla leader Jonas Savimbi is killed in clashes against government troops led by Angolan President José Eduardo dos Santos in Moxico Province, Angola.
Good Morning Afghanistan begins broadcasting over radio in Dari and Pashto, establishing a national news source for Afghanistan.

A mob attacks a train near Godhra, India, killing approximately 59 people. The state of Gujarat breaks out into riots, including the Gulbarg Society massacre on February 28 that kills approximately 69 people.
The Envisat environmental satellite is launched, with its purpose being the recording of information on environmental change.
10 – Afghan and coalition troops carry out Operation Anaconda in the Shah-i-Kot Valley, the largest combat operation against Al-Qaeda and the Taliban to that point.
Switzerland votes in favor of a referendum to join the United Nations, challenging a long-held tradition of neutrality and isolationism.
The Tribute in Light is installed at the World Trade Center site in New York City.

Sofia Gubaidulina's Johannes-Ostern is premiered, together with her earlier Johannes-Passion, at Hamburg's Michaeliskirche, performed by soloists, choir and orchestra from the Mariinsky Theatre combined with NDR choir and orchestra, conducted by Valery Gergiev.
In response to increasingly common attacks by Palestinian militants, Israeli initiates Operation Defensive Shield, a large-scale counter-terrorism operation in the West Bank.
Siege of the Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem: Israeli forces besiege the Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem when militants take shelter there. The siege will last for 38 days.
8 – Battle of Nablus: Israeli forces occupy Nablus, Palestine.
A peace agreement is made to end the Angolan Civil War.
The genome sequence for indica rice is published.

Llaguno Overpass events: a shootout takes place between the Caracas Metropolitan Police [es] and pro-government Bolivarian Circles in central Caracas, Venezuela, near the presidential Miraflores Palace, causing 19 deaths and injuring 127 people. The military high command refuse President Hugo Chávez's order to implement the Plan Ávila as a response to the protests and demands his resignation. President Chávez is subsequently arrested by the military. Chávez's request for asylum in Cuba is denied, and he is ordered to be tried in a Venezuelan court.
Augustin Bizimungu is arrested for his involvement in the Rwandan genocide.
President Hugo Chávez of Venezuela is restored to power following an attempted coup.
Romanian mathematician Preda Mihăilescu creates a proof for the Catalan's conjecture, which had gone unsolved for 158 years.
South African Mark Shuttleworth blasts off from the Baikonur Cosmodrome on the Soyuz TM-34, becoming the first African space tourist.: 453
Erfurt school massacre: An expelled student kills 16 people and commits suicide at a school in Erfurt, Germany.

Bojayá massacre: A church is struck with a cylinder bomb during a conflict between the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia and the United Self-Defense Forces of Colombia, killing an estimated 119 people.
NASA launches the Aqua satellite as part of the Earth Observing System.
2002 Kaspiysk bombing: Over 40 people are killed when insurgents bomb a military parade in Kaspiysk, Russia.
American FBI agent Robert Hanssen is sentenced to life in prison for espionage.
Rebels bombard Arthington, Liberia, with artillery during the Second Liberian Civil War causing panic in the neighboring capital, Monrovia.
Kaluchak massacre: Militants attack a bus and an Indian army camp in Kaluchak, Jammu and Kashmir, killing 31 people and escalating the India–Pakistan standoff.

Timor-Leste independence: East Timor regains its independence as the Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste after 2.5 years of United Nations administration and 26 years of Indonesian occupation since 1975.
Nepali Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba asks King Gyanendra to dissolve the parliament amid escalation of the Nepalese Civil War.
United States President George W. Bush and Russian President Vladimir Putin sign the Strategic Offensive Reductions Treaty.
The NATO-Russia Council is established.

The formal nine-month rescue and recovery operation at Ground Zero in New York City officially concluded with a solemn, largely silent ceremony, marking the completion of the removal of approximately 1.8 million tons of debris from the site following the September 11 attacks.
Archaeologists begin uncovering the Liye Qin Slips in Liye, China.
The Lennox Lewis vs. Mike Tyson boxing fight takes place. Following a scuffle prior to the match, Lennox Lewis defeats Mike Tyson.
British scientist Kevin Warwick carries out first direct electronic communication experiment between the nervous systems of two humans.
The ImClone stock trading case begins when ImClone Systems CEO Samuel D. Waksal is arrested for insider trading.
Russia withdraws from the START II nuclear reduction agreement with the United States.
2002 Bou'in-Zahra earthquake: A 6.5 magnitude earthquake strikes north-western Iran, killing over 200 people.
The WorldCom scandal breaks and the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission begins its investigation into WorldCom.

Second Battle of Yeonpyeong: During the 2002 FIFA World Cup in South Korea and Japan, two North Korean patrol boats cross a contested border in between the two Koreas and attack two South Korean Chamsuri-class patrol boats.

2002 FIFA World Cup: Brazil beats Germany 2–0 in the 2002 FIFA World Cup Final with Ronaldo scoring the two goals; Brazil's captain Cafu, who becomes the first player to appear in three successive World Cup finals, accepts the trophy on behalf of the team.
The Rome Statute comes into force, thereby establishing the International Criminal Court.
NASA launches the CONTOUR satellite but loses contact.
The Imperial War Museum North opens in Trafford, England.
Militants attack in Qasim Nagar, Jammu and Kashmir, killing 29 people.
The only captive baiji dolphin dies as the species approaches extinction.
The Machakos Protocol is signed during the Second Sudanese Civil War, establishing a framework for peace talks and possible independence of South Sudan.
At the height of the WorldCom scandal, WorldCom files the largest bankruptcy in American history.
Salvadoran generals José Guillermo García and Carlos Eugenio Vides Casanova are found liable for torture in an American court.
August 4 – The 2002 Commonwealth Games are held in Manchester, England.
The Sknyliv air show disaster takes place, killing 77, becoming the deadliest air show accident of all time.
The AKS primality test is published by Manindra Agrawal, Neeraj Kayal, and Nitin Saxena from the Indian Institutes of Technology.
2002 Khankala Mi-26 crash: Chechen separatists shoot down a Russian Mil Mi-26, killing 127 soldiers. It was the worst aviation disaster in the history of the Russian military.
September 4 – Typhoon Rusa, the most powerful typhoon to hit South Korea in 43 years, makes landfall, killing at least 236 people.
September 4 – Earth Summit 2002 takes places in Johannesburg, South Africa, aimed at discussing sustainable development by the United Nations.
EUMETSAT launches the Meteosat 8 satellite as part of its Meteosat program.
Switzerland joins the United Nations as the 190th member state after rejecting a place in 1986.
Yemeni al-Qaeda operative Ramzi bin al-Shibh is arrested in Pakistan for involvement in the September 11, 2001 attacks. He will later be found unfit to stand trial.
27 – Hurricane Isidore crosses Cuba, the Yucatán Peninsula, and Louisiana.
General Robert Guéï leads an army mutiny in an attempt to overthrow Ivory Coast President Laurent Gbagbo, resulting in civil war.
October 4 – Hurricane Lili crosses Cuba and several other Caribbean islands before making landfall in Louisiana.

The Senegalese ferry MV Le Joola sinks off the West African coast with 1,863 people killed according to official reports, making it one of the worst peacetime maritime disasters in history. Only 64 passengers survive.
East Timor is admitted to the United Nations as the 191st member state; it also changes its official longform name from "Democratic Republic of East Timor" to "Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste".
Former Republika Srpska president Biljana Plavšić pleads guilty to crimes against humanity for her involvement in the Bosnian genocide.
The genome sequences for malaria carriers anopheles gambiae and plasmodium falciparum are published.
The International Court of Justice rules in favor of Cameroon in Cameroon v. Nigeria.
The United States Congress approves military action in Iraq should it fail to comply with United Nations requirements for weapons of mass destruction.
Jemaah Islamiyah militants detonate multiple bombs in two nightclubs in Kuta, Bali, killing 202 people and injuring over 300 people, making it the worst terrorist act in Indonesia's history.
The Somali Reconciliation Conference begins, initiating peace talks between two factions of the Somali Civil War: the Transitional National Government and the government of Puntland.
The European Space Agency launches the INTEGRAL observatory.
The discovery of the James Ossuary is announced.
26 – Chechen rebels take control of the Nord-Ost theatre in Moscow and hold the audience hostage. At least 170 people are killed following a Russian attempt to subdue the militants.
2002 Brazilian general election: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is elected President of Brazil.
Belarus restricts religious activity outside of the Belarusian Orthodox Church with a new law.
2002 Denali earthquake: A 7.9 magnitude earthquake, one of the strongest North American earthquakes recorded, occurs in Alaska.: 181
A sovereignty referendum is held in Gibraltar. The people reject Spanish sovereignty.: 385
The United Nations Security Council unanimously adopts Resolution 1441, forcing Iraq to either disarm or face "serious consequences". Iraq agrees to the terms of the resolution on November 13.

Prestige oil spill: Greek oil tanker MV Prestige begins spilling oil off the coast of Galicia. It will continue until November 19, spilling 60,000 tonnes of oil in the worst environmental disaster in the history of the Iberian Peninsula.
Hu Jintao becomes General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party.
2002–2004 SARS outbreak: The first case of the Severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS) epidemic, a zoonosis caused by a coronavirus, is recorded in Guangdong province of south China.
Prague summit: NATO announces seven new countries that intend to join: Bulgaria, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Romania, Slovakia, and Slovenia.

2002 Mombasa attacks: Suicide bombers blow up an Israeli-owned hotel in Mombasa, Kenya, but their colleagues fail in their attempt to bring down an Arkia Israel Airlines charter flight with surface-to-air-missiles.
Opponents of President Chavez begin a strike in Venezuela.
The government of Burundi signs a ceasefire with the CNDD-FDD rebel group to end the Burundian Civil War. It holds until February 2003.
Shenzhou 4 is launched from China.
The United Nations Mission in Bosnia and Herzegovina ends.
